title: Three-dimensional hand marker sensitivity
timing: Added after assessment of the planar handle analysis to distinguish the body landmark measurement from the robot handle. The original handle scores and interpretation remain the prespecified primary test. This is exploratory and retrospective on the same previously accessed day and animal.
change: Use the three simultaneous shoulder-relative optical Marker_1 axes on the hand in place of the handle encoder throughout the history, labels, constant-velocity control, ridge fit and wrong-body control. Convert metres to centimetres before scaling. Four 50-ms pose tokens each contain XYZ position and within-token XYZ change, giving six pose features. Movement target is the 3D Euclidean displacement at +50/+100 ms from the last position, evaluated as Euclidean endpoint error. Use the same contact-count targets, source files, valid-data rule, causal processed timestamps, splits, three seeds, fixed optimizers, time schedule, parameter sharing, primary losses, uncertainty metrics, baselines, grouping, bootstrap and decision criterion from the primary protocol. The number of body coordinates alone changes the input/output linear layer sizes. No tuning or pooling with the primary result. Original upstream optical tracking/interpolation used later data; no online timing claim follows.
